text: Most people think Berkshire Hathaway's success is from the genius stockpicking of Warren Buffett, but that's only part of the story. Welcome back to Money Machines, where we break down how big money makes money. So Berkshire Hathaway is not your typical business. It's a holding company, which means it owns other companies, and it's a conglomerate, which means a lot of those businesses are not related. It's also decentralized, so these subsidiaries operate more or less autonomously, while headquarters is run by just under 30 people. And it also acts a little bit like a fund, in the sense that a big part of its strategy is investing in a portfolio of stocks. And this whole thing today is valued at over $1 trillion. Not bad for what started as a struggling textile company, but what's the Berkshire formula? It comes down to basically three engines. There's insurance, the businesses it owns, and it's iconic stock portfolio. So insurance is really the secret sauce of Berkshire Hathaway. That's why they own Geico and several other insurance and re-entrance companies, because they provide what's called float. Float is the money that an insurer holds between collecting premiums and paying out claims. Customers, individuals, businesses, even other insurance companies pay premiums up front, and then their claims get paid later. The money held in that gap is called the float. And this can be invested. And right now, Berkshire's float is about $178 billion. And you can make money from insurance in two ways. One is underwriting profit. So if your premiums are greater than your claims plus expenses, then you turn a profit. But you can also earn returns from the float that you invest. And this is the ultimate borrowing hack, because it's stable, low cost, or even zero cost, permanent capital, that you're essentially getting paid to hold if your underwriting is profitable. That brings us to our second engine. So if you have a big pile of cash, then you can use that capital to buy up more businesses. And that's essentially how Berkshire has become this sprawling conglomerate across manufacturing, utilities, railroads, retail, two of its biggest businesses are Biannese's, the major railroad company, but also Berkshire Hathaway Energy.
